column2: the writer's notes (doubts; where the article disagrees with the entry): for the data check

Entry says PhD in Munich in 1908; article says he graduated 4 November 1907 and the thesis was published 1908. Text gives only the 1908 publication. Entry's 'Allahabad Address of 1930' matches. Left out marriages, knighthood and Iran 1979 claim.
Entry says the Aztec Empire spread its use; consistent. Left out phonology tables, syntax examples and the Nawat/Pipil figures.
Article gives Hanseatic membership as 1402 and 1364; omitted. Entry says imperial residence under Charlemagne; text gives the 777 palace only.

Article truncated after the Second World War section; nothing said of 1946-47 beyond the lead. Entry says born Karachi; article 'likely' 25 December 1876, hedged. Left out the 1946 Calcutta Riots and Naidu's later remark.
Entry says Teutonic Order 1346; article says Livonian Order, so not named.

Article is thin; lists (stations, roads, teams) and pop culture left out. Entry says formed in 1871 from Sendai Domain; article says only 'formerly part of Mutsu', so not repeated. Statement that Sendai Castle belongs to Date Masamune's town is in the article. 'Rice and livestock ... fishing' from Economy section, placed in History loosely; editor may check. Population 2023 figure omitted.
Entry mentions the Gallic Veneti; not in article, not repeated. Article is short (about 440 words); present-day politics, prefect and population left out. Entry says prefecture at Vannes; consistent.
Consistent with entry.
Entry dates not repeated apart from 1844 and 1865, which agree.
Article: signed 24 August 1939, backdated to 23 August; entry says signed 23 August. Text says 'dated 23 August' and gives no signing day. Left out Gleiwitz, Katyn, the postwar border details.
Entry says British annexed 1853; article says only 'in the 19th century'; text follows the article.
Entry's Angkor and trade claims are not in the article; not repeated.
Article gives no bridge dates; entry's dates not repeated.
Entry says crown land of Habsburg monarchy; consistent.
Entry dates 1803-1815 fit article's main dating.
Entry's Thespiae Mouseia not in article text read.
Entry says first excavated 1920s, abandoned by about 1700 BCE, built about 2500 BCE; consistent.
Article is headed Kremlin (generic) but covers the Moscow Kremlin.

Entry calls Nayar a Cora ruler and gives 1884 Territory of Tepic; article calls Nayar a resistance leader and gives no 1884. Text does not name Nayar's role and does not mention 1884. Entry's 'separated from Jalisco' not in article. Population, rankings, tourism safety claims left out.
Entry says passport cancelled in 1960; article says the government prevented her return that year; text omits it. Entry's exile to 1990 consistent.

Article gives population 352,896 'as of 2025'; left out. Left out the 1661 uprising against Russian occupation to shorten. Article gives 'Tsar Aleksei Mikhailovitch'; spelled Mikhailovich. Left out: notable citizens, twin towns, sports, 2014 UNESCO consideration.

Article says first urbanised settlements c. 2000 BCE were by Canaanite, Amalekite, Amorite, Nabataean and Edomite groups; Nabataeans placed in 4th century BCE elsewhere in same article, so the list of groups was left out. Article contradicts itself on who built the Negev's runoff agriculture (Evenari thought Nabataeans; later studies Byzantine); wording follows later studies without naming Nabataeans for it. Left out: demography, Bedouin land disputes, environmental issues, solar power, wineries, fauna (present-day judgements or contested).

Article says 'about 400 years of Ottoman rule' in the lead but 241 years in the history section; 241 used, and 400 left out. Article gives two 2022 census figures for the city proper (178,976 and 182,797) and two for the administrative area; wrote 'fewer than 200,000' and no area figure. Article calls Stevan Sremac a native of Niš but elsewhere says he came shortly after liberation; left out. Constantine omitted from the emperors list because the entry already gives him.

Entry gives Benedictine community 966; article does not date it, so not repeated. Article says Treaty of Compiègne gave Cotentin/Avranchin to Bretons but that these lands were never really part of Brittany; left out. Article says island 'remained unconquered during the Hundred Years' War'; omitted. Left out: tourism figures, population, economy, popular culture, 2014 bridge.

Article says Wadiyar dynasty capital 1399 to 1947 and also Seringapatam capital from 1610; entry says 1399 'according to tradition' and capital again after 1799. Text avoids a capital date for Mysore itself. Spelling Wodeyar/Wadiyar varies in article; Wodeyar used as in entry. Left out: demographics, economy rankings, transport, sister cities.

Entry's 1363 siege and Zhu Wenzheng are not in the article; not repeated. Article says Nanchang Uprising 'succeeded in holding the city for only a few days'; wording follows it. Article's Wang Bo text is called a classic 'Tengwang Ge Xu'; written as in article. Left out: economy, GDP, transport figures, rankings, food, notable people.

Article calls Carchemish 605 BC; entry also 605 BCE. Failed Egypt invasion dated 601 BC elsewhere in article; left undated here. Article does not date Jerusalem's fall to a month; 587 BCE as in article (some other sources say 586; not used). Article relies on Berossus for wife Amytis; stated here only as tradition's Hanging Gardens link. Left out: titles, name debate, Josephus's accounts, al-Ṭabarī.

Article gives Finnic migration 'twelve thousand years BC' alongside sites 'up to nine thousand years old'; left out. Article has an inconsistent dating of river's origin (2000 BC vs 1410-1250 BC); both given as article's own attribution (older books vs recent research). Left out: pollution, hydrography numbers, bridges list, pipelines, flora and fauna, 1963 aircraft incident.

Article says first casino opened in La Condamine in 1862; entry says Charles III founded its casino in 1863 and named the quarter in 1866. Casino years left out; only the 1856 concession is given. Left out: films, literature, music, hotel room counts, population, twin cities.

Article says Narbo Martius was capital of Gallia Transalpina, later renamed Narbonensis; entry says capital of Gallia Narbonensis. Wording follows the article and is consistent with the entry. Article's Elisyces identification of Montlaurès is disputed; left out. Article calls Frankish defeat of Amalaric 531 and Septimania 'the only territory from Gaul to fend off Franks'; left out as detail. Left out: sport, personalities, transport, twin towns.

Article's lead says 'abandoned violence in the 1970s' and elsewhere that the Brotherhood 'does not have a clear ideological platform on violence'; the text attributes the 1970s claim to Foreign Affairs authors. Left out as present-day or contested: terrorist designations by governments, Qatar/Gulf relations, classification approaches, Australian street gang, Indonesian PKS figures, criticism section, status of non-Muslims, controversy on 2013 events. Article says al-Banna 'accepted the utility of political violence' and members carried out assassinations including El Nokrashy 1948; already in the entry, so not repeated.

Article says Neptune 'likely' associated with freshwater before the sea; wording kept as hedged. Left out: Dumézil/Preller/Petersmann theological debates in detail, Etruscan Liver of Piacenza, Consus identification, mirrors. Article's temple dating: 'at least 206 BC' kept.

Article says Ruttledge thought the mountain about 6,000 m; entry says 6,638 m; the height from Ruttledge is left out. Left out: geology, climate, ICIMOD project, pilgrimage logistics after 2015, COVID suspension.

Entry says created 1994 from the eastern Transvaal; article says merged with former homelands as well; text includes both without contradiction. Left out: post-apartheid land redistribution and corruption claims, governance, pollution, economy figures, species lists.

Article's decline dates conflict (destruction c. 1200 vs c. 1150); destruction stated only as around 1200 BCE, as in entry. Article says Schliemann's shaft graves 'from c. 1600 BC' and Circle A sixteenth century BC; entry says 17th and 16th century; text says Circle A sixteenth century and Circle B c. 1650-1550. Article places the site both near the Saronic Gulf and the Gulf of Argolis; gulf omitted. Left out: myths of Perseid and Atreid dynasties, religion, excavations after 1902.

Article does not say how or where he died, so no 'Death and legacy' section; entry dates c. 1141–1209 are used only by the entry. Article dates of poems differ between sources (Makhzan 1163 or 1176; Eskandar-Nameh 1194 or 1196-1202); both given as the article gives them. Article says he is believed to have lived whole life in the South Caucasus; entry says Persian poet from Ganja in the Caucasus. Entry mentions Akhsitan I and the Eldiguzids, not in the part of the article provided; not repeated. Left out: nationality debates, modern commemorations, Western reception, banknotes.

Birth year uncertain (597, 603 or 605) per article; none printed in text except as the article's range. Article says the Cyprus raid year is unclear (647-650); left undated. Article's lead says Ali's assassination in 661 and Hasan's abdication; entry says 'after Ali's death'. Left out: Siege of Constantinople details, Syrian tribal politics, assassination claims against Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid, poisoning of Hasan accusation.

Article does not describe al-Idrisi's death, so no 'Death and legacy' section. Article lead says born 1100, died 1165; entry says c. 1100–c. 1165 and 'born probably in Ceuta'; text says 'believed to have been born in Ceuta in 1100'. Left out: Andalusian-American contact theories, Pluto feature, popular culture, Greenland/Ireland passage. Article says 18 years at court before the map of 1154; arrival year not given and not printed.

Entry says it joined the Swiss Confederation as a canton in 1815 and became a republic 1848; article lead says 1848 republic and canton, and the article section on 1814 is cut off. The article's lead says Neuchâtel became a canton in 1848; entry says 1815, so the canton date is left out of the text. Entry says first recorded 1011; text consistent. Left out: demographics, politics, crime, sports, notable people.

Article's lead gives death 28 March 1881 (O.S. 16 March); the text says 'a week after his 42nd birthday' as in the article body. Article says Mussorgsky's decline and alcoholism; included plainly, no moralising. Left out: name spelling, quotations on reputation, popular culture, Alexander III crossing off Boris.
Article's own 1945 detail: whole city centre had to be rebuilt; Oroku merged 1 Sep 1954 (not used for length). Article says Shuri Castle used as Japanese command post; omitted.

Article says city founded 791 AD by Harun al-Rashid; entry gives no date; Founding date 791 is the article's. Article gives house count 3,000 to 30 'by the start of 16th century' while Texeira 1604 - omitted.
Article gives length 544 km, entry 545 km: no length printed. Article details on Allied crossing of Nancy trimmed; says Nancy liberated 15 September.
Article is short; two sections. Entry says 'founded under Justinian I', article only says 6th-century.
Article gives caves 1st c. BCE to 2nd c. CE; entry says 3rd century CE: end date omitted. Article says Jackson 'assassinated'; worded as article.

Article says monks certainly there since 4th c., possibly 3rd; entry says hermits from at least 9th c.: omitted dates of earliest monks. Article says Mary 'out of bounds to all other women' - tradition.
Pribina/833/880 facts of the entry not in the article body read; omitted.
Article says Caesar's assembly 53 BC and also 50 BCE for mention: used 53 BCE only for assembly.
Article says wooden church then Vakhtang's basilica survived to the 11th c.; Svetitskhoveli listed as 11th century; kept brief. 'Holy City' declaration 2014 omitted.
Article's embezzlement, INDEC and ideology sections left out as contested/judgement. Legacy section of article not read.

Article gives cardinal 1448 or 1449; entry no year: not printed. Ordering note: 'He wrote that after the Fall...' needs reading; article says 'Shortly after the Fall of Constantinople in 1453, Nicholas wrote De pace fidei'. Earth as a star claim is from a quoted Catholic Encyclopedia passage about his astronomical views. Imprisoned by Sigismund, 'Duke of Austria' in article vs 'of Tyrol' in entry: used 'Duke Sigismund of Austria' as article - mild difference, fine.
Entry: married into Loharu family; Delhi residence; account of 1857 - not in the portions read; not printed. Article's 'Calcutta journey' appears twice; once used.
Article contains Togakure legend (12th c.) not used; Shimabara quote omitted. Entry says 15th-16th c.; article agrees.
Article does not contain 'peace for our time' in portion read; not printed.
Article lead says Constantinople siege 1422, body says 1421: no year printed. Entry's Germiyanid inheritance 1429 vs article 'annexed' states (no year): no year printed. Kosovo 1448 not in read part.
Article says Multan 'sixth-largest city' - ranking, omitted. Entry says Ranjit Singh captured 1818: I printed 'Sikh Empire ruled it from 1818 to 1849' as the article.
Entry says five brothers strangled on accession; article says same. Not repeated. Battle of Sisak 1593 omitted. Death not read.
Article says Riyadh capital 'since 1824' (second Saudi state). Entry mentions nothing conflicting.
Length 937 km in article vs 'about 900' in entry: not printed. Article says Neman 'largest' etc.
Left out wildlife lists beyond a few species. Description says the Masmughans sheltered here; the article does not mention them, so not repeated.

The article says the 1006 eruption is claimed to have caused the collapse of the Hindu Kingdom of Mataram, evidence insufficient; the entry says Medang moved in 929 possibly after eruptions. Left the collapse claim out so the page does not disagree with the entry. Left out eruptions after 2010 (recent).

Article says Armenian-held Taron came to Bagratids in late 8th century; entry mentions Mamikonian and Bagratid, not contradicted. Population figure for 2022 is the article's; kept as a rounded fact with year.

Article gives birth as 6 August 1698 or 22 November 1688; left out. Article attributes the 1738 Kandahar conquest in two places; kept 1738. Entry says reigned 1736-1747, matches. Left out the Delhi sack details (not in the excerpt given).

Entry says excavations of Herculaneum and Pompeii from 1738 and 1748; article gives no dates for these, so none printed. Entry says movement from mid-18th century; article says visual arts c.1760 and Italian neoclassicism c.1750; both given loosely. Left out non-European detail.
Entry says it passed to Mecklenburg around 1300 with the Lordship of Stargard; article says 1292 without the Stargard detail. Left the year out. Left out sports, twin towns, mayor, notable people.
Article gives the Hemudu date as 4800 BCE in the lead and 5000-4500 BCE in the history; left the date out. Left out economy rankings, GDP, officials, metro, transport.
Article says Minos conversed with Zeus every nine years, matches entry. The article explicitly says there is no evidence Minos was real; entry says legendary: consistent.

Entry says Nanbu moved their seat at the end of the 16th century and built Morioka Castle in stages; article says Nanbu built Kozukata Castle in 1592, renamed Morioka Castle later. Printed no year for the building to avoid disagreement. Left out transport, sport, notable people.
Entry says about 360 km; article 362 km, consistent. Entry says rises near Villingen-Schwenningen; article says Schwenningen; consistent. Left out power plants, locks detail, renaturation.
Entry: head of state of Soviet Russia from 1919 and of USSR from 1922; article: same post from 1919, renamed in 1922. Consistent.
Entry says eruption around 946, one of the largest of the past two thousand years; article says the last 5,000 years. Left the ranking out. Left out the 2010s eruption research and current disputes.

Entry says he bought towns from the Hamidids and defeated Serbs on the Maritsa; article gives neither, only the 1371 defeat of Vukasin. Article gives 29 June 1326; entry c. 1326; no birth date printed. Article states 'the Serbs, Bulgarians, Albanians, Hungarians' fought; kept.

Entry says left bank of the Oka; article says west bank. Bank left out. Entry says princes of the Chernigov line; article does not say so; not repeated. Article is short (665 words); text is near the lower bound.
Entry says Crusader royal domain and lordship; article says royal domain. Left out all modern politics, intifadas, mayors.
Entry says the Bolsheviks crushed the movement in 1921; article consistent. Left out events from 2022 onward.

Article says Navajo Nation has 427,414 enrolled citizens as of 2026; given as 'more than 427,000' without 'as of'. Article gives name origin both from Spanish missionaries re Pueblo and from Tewa; used the Tewa derivation only. Left out uranium mining, modern media, notable people.

Entry says Albert of Mainz; article says Archbishop Albert of Brandenburg and also of Mainz; I wrote Albert of Brandenburg as the article does mostly. Entry says Castle Church; article says All Saints' Church; consistent as same church.

Entry says about 65 m; article gives 62 or 65 m: height left out. Article's date of inscription is uncertain (1193/4 or 1174/5 in one place); used only the Kufic reading of 590 AH given in the inscription section. Left out conservation and security issues of recent years.
Entry says founded by Spain in 1770; article says 1774 by Portola and Serra. Left out founding date and founders. Left out government, economy, sports.

Article says the Carmelites were founded in 1209 and the Rule dates from about 1210; entry says early 13th century, compatible. Article's Ottoman and Druze settlement dates are vague and were left out.

Article gives the Ottoman takeover as 1463 (list) and 1465 (text), and the renaming Onogošt to Nikšić as mid-15th century, first recorded 1518, official 1767: left all of these out. Entry says Congress of Berlin 1878; article says Treaty of Berlin, I used Treaty of Berlin without a year.

Article is inconsistent on the end of the Syrian wars and on when hereditary rule was secured (peace 1842; 'after 1843 ... Treaty of Balta Liman'; hereditary rule secured in 1846 visit): all left out. The article does not mention Diriyah; entry's 1818 not repeated. Bulaq press date given in article as 1819/21.

Article dates: 1570-1544 BC for the start, Nineteenth Dynasty 1295-1189 yet Ramesses I's accession 1292; entry says about 1550 BCE to about 1070 BCE. No start/end years printed. Article says 16th to 11th century BC. Legacy section is short (below 40 words in one paragraph? it is about 55).

SKIPPED: article has under 250 words of history (one battle of 1342); mostly tourism, schools, climate and a list of natives; entry's 1522 sack and linen trade are not in it Article: Battle of Morlaix 30 September 1342 (Hundred Years' War, English under William de Bohun, Earl of Northampton, against Charles, Duke of Brittany), viaduct 1861-1863, Maison de la duchesse Anne begun in the 1520s.

Article says Tambora and Pekat kingdoms nowhere; entry names them, not repeated. Death toll: at least 71,000 (article), entry says tens of thousands; compatible. Left out the 2025-2026 unrest section.
Article gives duration both as six weeks and up to late March 1938; entry says about six weeks; both reflected as the article gives them. Article says Matsui recalled February 1938; left out.
Plotinus c. 205-270 vs c. 205-271; Porphyry c. 232 vs 233 in the article: dates of death/birth omitted. Article says Plotinus's possible Indian influence; left out.
Article: reigned 8 Nov 1933 until deposed 17 July 1973; abdication letter August 1973. Article's 'last king of Afghanistan' etc. not conflicting. Left out his remarks on US pressure and Pakistan.

Article: Bhutto executed less than two years after sentence; no execution date given in the section text. I printed no date for it. Left out economic claims (GDP growth) and aid figures, popular-culture portrayals. Article says the Afghan mission was 'backed by the United States and Saudi Arabia'.

Article says Nalanda operated from 427 to around 1400; entry says 5th to 12th century, so no end date is printed. Article's section headings follow its own place/people/institution; I used the 'Organisation and way of life' heading though the entry type is place (guide lists it for institutions).

Article gives the coup as 1 November and Diem's death as 2 November 1963; entry says November 1963. Article says Diem returned June 1954 and was appointed prime minister on 26 June, entry says 1954. Left out the claims about Diem's personalist philosophy detail and honours.

Article gives the peak as 1,545 m (commonly reported) and 1,532.7 m; entry says about 1,530 m. No height printed. Inscription and step counts vary within the article; only the 6,660 figure kept. Entry says Qin Shi Huang and Emperor Wu of Han performed the sacrifices; article attributes the Han sacrifices generally and Wu Di only to the cypresses.

Entry says taken around 1207 by the Ghisi; article says occupied 1204 by Andrea Ghisi and castle built 1207: no date printed for the occupation, and the 1207 refers to the castle as the article gives it. Left out popular culture and tourism trivia.

Article dates its start as capital 1827 (lead) and 1829 (Kapodistrias made it official capital): start year omitted. Article says Venetian domination 1338-1540 (architecture) vs 1388 purchase: 1338 omitted. Entry mentions Leo Sgouros; not in article, not repeated.

Article's 9th-century lambskin glove production and 19th-century development both given; entry says town later became centre of glove-making. Article's 1112 passage is garbled (Beranger III 'father of the future King of Aragon'): kept as given. Left out the 1999 McDonald's protest and fiction.

Article gives the coup date only as 28 Mordad 1332 in the lead; entry says August 1953, so I wrote 'August 1953'. Left out the 2013 US acknowledgement, family section and popular culture. The British oil boycott in the entry is not in the article.
Entry says the lands below were part of Etiuni attacked by Urartu in the 9th-8th centuries BCE; not in the article, not repeated.
Entry gives c. 1960; article gives 1950-1962 (uncertain), so the text says the year is uncertain. Dates of the loss of his eye differ (1986, 1987, 1989): omitted. Left out events after 2015 (2021).
Entry says Alaeddin Mosque built 1223 and mentions Tuwana; neither is in the article, so only '13th century' is used.

Article gives 100,000 Jews deported by Horthy's permission and also 437,000 deported to Auschwitz in late 1944 (lead); not printed beyond the 100,000 attributed figure. Article says Germans invaded in March 1944; entry says deposed in October 1944, consistent.
Article says 29 June 1520 death date in lead; text says 'probably'. Entry's 1502 matches the article's most likely year. Article says the Florentine Codex; omitted.

Article calls Narmer Early Dynastic; entry says last of Dynasty 0, article says peak 'during Dynasty 0 through the reign of Narmer' - not asserted. 'Raging catfish' is the article's 'sometimes translated'. Neithhotep omitted (doubtful).
Article gives two areas for the lines (50 km2 and 450 km2); omitted. Entry says some 70 figures; article says more than 70.

Entry says the valley was the centre of Great Moravia in the 9th century; the article does not mention Great Moravia, so omitted. Article says upper river is in 'north-eastern corner of Pardubice Region'; entry says north of Czech Republic.

Entry says 'Ilona Zrínyi defended it 1685 to 1688' - article only mentions Thököly's revolt 1685-1688 for the castle; Zrinyi omitted. Entry says passed to Czechoslovakia in 1920: article says 4 June 1920 consistent. Article says Czechoslovakia re-established then Soviet 1945 treaty; text simplified.
Article's Wilber explanation of the orientation is given as fact in text; it is a 'most plausible explanation' in the article - hedge not added; consider. Article says Abbas 'the Great'.

Entry says 1933-1939; article gives 1938 as the last new legislation; text avoids end date. Article describes First New Deal as 1933 to 1935 in lead but 1933-34 in heading; text says 'up to 1935' and Second 'from 1935'. Article's mention of 14.3% May 1937 to 19.0% June 1938 used.
Entry says massacre ordered 88 BCE - matches. Article says suicide after Pharnaces rebelled; text keeps. Entry's 'taking Lesser Armenia' not in article, left out. 'Last war against Pompey' fine.
Entry mentions Frankish lords of Salona; article does not, omitted. Article says Palmer's theory is considered strong but unsupported; text states both.

Entry says island governed by New York until 1692 passed to Massachusetts Bay; article says Dukes County, New York, until 17 Oct 1691 charter, new governor arrived 14 May 1692: dates left out. Entry says 'leading centre of American whaling' - article does not say this; not repeated.

Entry's mention of Pulakeshin II halting Harsha is not in the article; omitted. Article says 'only river in the world venerated through a parikrama' - omitted as unreliable. Article calls it traditional boundary between North and South India; entry says north India and Deccan.
Entry mentions Touro Synagogue and Jewish community; article does not, omitted. Entry says 'leading ports of colonial America'; article says major 18th-century port.

Entry says Rif War ended 'with French help'; article: 1925 combined action, victory 1927. Article calls him 'dictator' with 'prime minister 1923-1930'. Article says 'Alhucemas landing' in lead; omitted.

Article gives Mount Halcon as 2,586 m and in the list 2,616 m; omitted. Entry says Mangyan peoples live in interior; text keeps general. Article's Spanish conquest paragraph is garbled (Legazpi, Salcedo); detail left out.

Entry says 'nearly 500 temples ... 4th to 14th century'; article lead says 500 temples and 735 caves now exist; text uses 735/487/248 from article's Caves section. UNESCO 1987 not in article, omitted. Stein's account omitted.
Article says 'Russian soldiers occupied in 1814' - omitted. Entry says basilica 'partly in expiation' - article says gesture of expiation for suffering of France in the war; text gives that.
Entry gives 'about 2,814 metres'. Article's Israel/Syria control sections after 1974 and the 2024 summit item left out as recent and contested. Knohl and Transfiguration claims left out as doubtful.

Article gives pact as 1745 in one section and 1744-1746 in another; entry says 1744: year left out ('mid-1740s'). Entry says Banu Khalid emir pressured expulsion; article only says 'expulsion from Uyayna', not who; omitted. Article gives Emirate of Diriyah 'established in 1727' - omitted. Capture of Riyadh '1773' vs '1773-4' - printed 'in 1773 or 1774' as article does. Article sentence about the present-day state of Saudi Arabia omitted.

Entry says imperial city from late 12th century until 1802; article says Freie Reichsstadt from mid-13th century: dates left out. Entry says Hanseatic League member; article does not, omitted. Entry says Müntzer made it his base; article says he preached there from August 1524. Article also says Müntzer and Pfeiffer were Anabaptists; omitted.
Article says Lebak appointment 1857; desc says he resigned 1856: year left out.
Article lead gives Finance 1969-1981, body 1982: end year left out. Corruption and ethnic-elite judgements omitted. EDITOR: the presidency moved under Career (a president has no Reign).

Article says Lady Mo; desc Thao Suranari (same person).

Colony date (desc 299 BCE) not given in article; left out.

Church story hedged as in article. Desc: al-Hakam II 'in the 960s'; article mihrab finished 971.

Article's ordinal count of successful censure motions includes 2024 and 2025 events; left out as recent. Article lists 'Fourth Republic' heading empty; nothing added. Salaries, eligibility, procedure left out.

The Louise Temple 'to house the tomb' is the article's wording; actually phrasing kept. Irma Grese, notable people, festival omitted.

Entry mentions the 1969 ANC Morogoro Conference and Mazimbu college; the article does not, so omitted. Article has little early history; two sections only. Sister cities, APOPO rats, USAID programme omitted.

Left out Freemasonry section including anti-Jewish writings in Tafsir al-Manar; the editor may want it recorded. Article attributes 'I went to the West...' quote; not used.

Article says Vasco da Gama time sultan; entry 1498; used no date. Fort São Sebastião: article '16th century', entry doesn't date it.

Article: Tobacco Protest 1890-1891 (lead) vs entry 1891-1892; date omitted, only 1890 concession given as article body says.
